title: Multiclot in Acute and Perioperative Medicine: Analysis of Routinely Measured Viscoelastic Coagulation Parameters in Clinical Care
summary:
During heart surgery, blood clotting can become impaired. This may lead to increased bleeding and sometimes makes it necessary to give patients blood products. To allow doctors to quickly assess whether blood clotting is working properly, rapid clotting tests are used in the operating room. These tests show within a few minutes how well the blood is clotting and help the treatment team decide whether medications or blood products are needed. In addition, blood samples are sent to the laboratory, but those results take longer to become available.
At University Hospital Bonn, a new device for these rapid clotting tests is being used in routine care. It replaces a previously used device that is no longer reliably available in the long term. The treatment concept and decisions made at the patient's bedside remain unchanged.
This study aims to examine how closely the results of the new device match those of the laboratory tests. It will also examine whether the device can reliably detect whether a blood-thinning medication used during surgery is still active in the body after a counteracting medication has been given.
The study uses only data that arise during normal medical care. No additional examinations, no additional blood draws, and no changes in treatment will be performed. Approximately 60 patients will be evaluated over a period of twelve months.
conditions: Perioperative haemostatic disorders and coagulopathies in cardiac surgery patients, including functional fibrinogen disturbances and residual heparin effects following protamine administration in the context of cardiopulmonary bypass.

interventions.name: Observation of cardiac surgery patients under routine care with perioperative viscoelastic coagulation monitoring (Multiclot®) and parallel standard laboratory coagulation testing. No study-related intervention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Performing cardiac surgery, conducting viscoelastic and coagulation testing as part of routine clinical practice
Exclusion criteria:
No Multiclot testing performed, No coagulation testing performed
